prompt: Why does BERT-style masked language modelling read context on both sides of a gap?
options: Because the mask token is placed at the end of the sequence
Because the model sees the whole sequence, so a masked word can be predicted from the words before and after it
Because the model reads backwards
Because masking removes the need for context
explanation: The encoder attends in both directions, so the words after a gap are as available as the words before it.

prompt: A pooled vector averages over padding positions. What goes wrong?
options: Nothing, padding is always zero
The representation of a text depends on how much padding its batch needed, so the same text can get different predictions
The softmax stops working
The learning rate must be lowered
explanation: Padding changes the average, so the same text gets different vectors in different batches. Pooling must use only the real tokens.

prompt: Why is NER scored at the span level rather than the token level?
options: Token scores are impossible to compute
Most tokens are outside any entity, so token accuracy hides errors on the entities themselves
Spans are always longer than tokens
Span scores are always higher
explanation: Token accuracy is dominated by the O tags. Span F1 measures whether each entity is found with the right boundaries and label.

prompt: A dataset has 98% negative examples. A model that always predicts negative has high accuracy. Which metric exposes the failure?
options: Accuracy, since it is high
Recall on the positive class, or macro-F1
The number of tokens
The learning rate
explanation: Recall on the rare class, and macro-F1, reveal that the model finds none of the positives, which accuracy hides.

prompt: Why should oversampling a rare class happen after the train/test split?
options: Because oversampling is slower after the split
Because duplicates of the same text on both sides of the split inflate the test scores
Because the test set must be balanced by design
Because the split creates the classes
explanation: Copies of a text in both training and test data let the model memorize answers it will be tested on, so the score is optimistic.
